### 01 · CRUD basics: native Java client vs. GemFire for gRPC
Both clients are small HTTP services with the same `/crud` API. Load comes from **k6** (`make load`), and each run shows up as a shaded annotation. **native-java**: `ClientCache` through the locator, PR single-hop. **grpc-java**: plaintext channel straight to `server1:50051`. *End-to-end* = the HTTP request as k6 saw it. *GemFire call* = time inside the gRPC RPC / Region API call, measured in the client.

panels.title: At a glance (GemFire calls made by each client)
Throughput
panels.description: Successful GemFire calls per second, per client (driven by k6).

panels.title: Demo checks
panels.description: Assertions from the narrated demo (runs at client startup and on POST /demo): ✓ passed, ✗ failed. Any failure turns red.

panels.title: Load test (k6): end-to-end vs. GemFire call
Requests/s (k6)
panels.description: Requests k6 completed per second, per target client. Filter runs with the `run` variable.

panels.title: p50: end-to-end vs. GemFire call
panels.description: Solid = end-to-end (k6), dashed = GemFire call (in the client). The gap between a client's two lines is HTTP + app overhead. That overhead is the same code in both clients, so the GemFire call is where they differ.

panels.title: p99: end-to-end vs. GemFire call
panels.description: Solid = end-to-end (k6), dashed = GemFire call (in the client). The gap between a client's two lines is HTTP + app overhead. That overhead is the same code in both clients, so the GemFire call is where they differ.

panels.description: VUs climb when a client can't keep up with an arrival-rate script.

panels.title: Per-operation latency (last 5 minutes)
panels.description: gRPC ÷ native > 1 means gRPC is slower. Native GetAndPut, Remove and GetAndRemove are two round trips: client put()/remove() don't return the old value. See the README mapping table.

panels.description: Pick operations with the `op` variable at the top of the dashboard.

panels.description: gRPC: status code. Native: exception class. Flat zero = no errors.

targets.expr: sum by (client, code) (rate(demo_errors_total[1m])) or sum by (client) (rate(demo_op_latency_seconds_count[1m])) * 0

panels.title: GemFire servers: what the cluster sees
Puts forwarded to the owning server
panels.description: PartitionedRegionStats.putRemoteCompleted: puts that arrived at a server that doesn't own the bucket and had to be forwarded. The gRPC client sends everything to server1, so about half its writes take this extra hop. Native single-hop sends each op straight to the owner.

panels.title: Client connections per server
panels.description: native: CacheServerStats.currentClientConnections (pooled sockets). gRPC: GrpcServerStats.grpc.server.connections (one multiplexed HTTP/2 connection). The only statistic the gRPC extension registers.

panels.title: Cache-server (native protocol) requests/s
panels.description: CacheServerStats counts only native-protocol traffic on port 40404. gRPC requests don't pass through the cache server, so they don't show up here.

panels.title: CPU: GemFire members (cores)
panels.description: server1 is the gRPC entry point. It also decodes protobuf and forwards requests for buckets it doesn't own.

panels.title: Client CPU per operation
panels.description: Client container CPU-seconds ÷ ops completed. Lower is cheaper.
